subject: Clarification on training guarantees, retention windows, and erase mapping
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finedge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: do you train on customer text? + retention windows

Hi Ben,

We're doing our security review for Redwood as part of an upcoming pilot. I have a handful of specific items we need explicit answers for so our InfoSec and Legal teams can sign off: 

1) "Do you ever train your models on customer-provided text?" Please be explicit about the default behavior for hosted API customers, and whether any downstream experiments could ingest our content.
2) Which data types are retained (request/response payloads, logs, metrics, KV caches, debug snapshots, backups)? Give default retention windows and whether they're configurable.
3) For backups/snapshots: are they included in any training or derivative pipelines? How are they identified/segregated?
4) Deletion/erase: if we request deletion for all PII + customer text, what is the timeline and proof? Do you provide an "erase certificate"?
5) Contract language: can you provide a short clause we can include in our contract that guarantees non-training of our customer text and describes retention/TTL behaviors?

Also, we may request SOC2 artifacts. Appreciate a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Security Lead, FinEdge
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 13:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: do you train on customer text? + retention windows

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and we can schedule a call if you'd like.

TL;DR:
- Redwood does not include customer request/response text in our model training pipelines by default.
- Hosted API: transient telemetry (traces and limited debug logs) retained for 7 days by default; full request/response traces kept only when needed for debugging and then purged within 30 days unless the customer requests an extension.
- Backups/snapshots are subject to a separate TTL (30 days default) and are not used for model training.
- We provide an erase confirmation after a completed purge; for enterprise accounts we can issue a signed eradication certificate.

Details:
1) Training flows: Our central training systems are logically and procedurally segregated from tenant request stores. We do not route customer-provided plain-text requests into model training datasets unless there is an explicit, documented opt-in (e.g., a joint research experiment or a data-sharing addendum signed by both parties). That opt-in is rare and requires legal signoff.

2) Data types & retention: 
- Request/response traces: default 7 days (configurable).
- Debug snapshots and full traces taken for incident triage: retained up to 30 days and then deleted unless retained by agreement.
- Audit logs / billing records: retained longer for compliance (90 days to 1 year depending on subscription tier).
- KV caches and ephemeral execution state: kept in-memory or on-disk for runtime only; persisted snapshots are rotated and expire 7-30 days depending on environment.

3) Backups & snapshots: Backups are encrypted, tagged with tenant IDs, and covered by access controls. They are not fed into any model training or evaluation pipelines. Any retention of backups follows our backup TTL policy (30 days by default for hosted) and can be shortened or excluded for customers under Dedicated or Private deployments.

4) Deletion & proof: We support targeted erase requests for tenant data. Standard deletion timeline is 30 days end-to-end (coordinate with retention offsets for backups). For Dedicated/Private customers we can negotiate faster windows. When deletion completes we issue a confirmation email; for enterprise customers that includes a signed eradication statement with time-stamped logs showing purge operations.

5) Contract snippet (informal):
"Vendor shall not use Customer-provided content, including but not limited to request and response payloads, logs, or debug artifacts, as training data for Vendor's models or for derivative model development unless Customer has provided prior written consent in a separate addendum. Vendor will retain Customer content only as necessary to provide service and for the retention periods specified in the Agreement, and will comply with Customer requests to delete Customer content within the timelines agreed in the Agreement."

Attachments: Marissa has a draft clause and a retention diagram she can share. If you want, we can add language about snapshots and backups to the clause.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Clarify: do you train on customer text? + retention windows

Priyom — quick internal check before I finalize the language to FinEdge: can you confirm the following for hosted API (defaults) so I don't overpromise?
1) Default request/response trace TTL = 7 days.
2) Incident snapshots / debug traces TTL = up to 30 days, removed after triage.
3) Backups TTL = 30 days and never used for training.
4) KV cache: ephemeral; persisted snapshots rotated and expire within 7 days unless the customer elects otherwise.

Also confirm that we have an internal template for a signed eradication certificate for Enterprise customers and the log proof we include.

If anything above is wrong, flag changes and I won't send final clause.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finedge.com>, Legal Team <legal@finedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: do you train on customer text? + retention windows

Hi Samir / FinEdge Legal — following up with a consolidated response and the requested artifacts. Attached: redwood_nontrain_clause_v1.docx (proposed contract language) and log_retention_diagram.png (visual TTLs). Also linking our public docs and the HubSpot record: https://hub.redwood.ai/deals/DEAL-8491

Key commitments (finalized):
- Non-training guarantee: Redwood will not use FinEdge customer-provided text, logs, debug snapshots, backups, or KV cache contents for the purposes of training or improving our public or private models unless FinEdge provides explicit written consent.
- Default retention (hosted): request/response traces = 7 days; debug snapshots = up to 30 days (only when captured for triage); backups = 30 days. Audit logs/billing records retained per subscription tier (90–365 days).
- Erasure: Standard erase requests are processed end-to-end within 30 days. For Dedicated or Private customers we will negotiate shorter windows and provide a signed eradication certificate that includes time-stamped deletion logs.

If you want us to remove request/response traces entirely during the pilot (zero retention on hosted), we can enact that change immediately for the pilot period and document it in the MPA.

Next steps: 1) Review the attached clause and mark any redlines; 2) confirm whether you want the pilot zero-retention option; 3) schedule Legal sync (we're available Tue 19 Aug 11:00 PT).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this wrapped up.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
